clue.text: Sportspeople seeing injuries including leaderless crew, flailing rowers

flailing limbs thrash about wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: welts are raised marks on the skin from a blow
the word with its first letter removed
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A rowing team, flailing badly, ends up covered in cuts and bruises.
explanation.walkthrough: WELTS opens to take in ERW (the shuffled REW) followed by EIGHT, giving WELT-ERW-EIGHT-S. 'Crew' looks like the rowing word, but the rowing crew is clued by 'rowers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Welterweights are boxers or wrestlers competing in a particular weight class, so they are sportsmen and women.

clue.text: Amusing Western, A Horse Is Hot

taken as written
gee-gee, a childish word for a horse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film critic praising a comic cowboy movie called 'A Horse Is Hot'.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make 'A Horse Is Hot' look like a film title, and 'Western' like its genre; each word is really a separate piece. GG (gee-gee) is a crossword staple for horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Waggish describes someone playfully humorous, like a wag or joker, so it is a synonym for funny.

clue.text: Composer's catalogue in the auditorium

blocks.note: a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A concert-goer reading a composer's list of works while seated in the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer's' reads as possessive, but the 's is 'is': the composer is the catalogue, when heard. Franz Liszt's name is said exactly like 'list'.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a celebrated Hungarian pianist and writer of Romantic music, an example of the category.

clue.text: Delivering 'second-to-last' finales

indicators.note: read as an instruction, 'S to last' sends the leading letter round to the end

blocks.note: sending something is delivering it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-to-last' looks like penultimate, but it splits as S (second) to last: the S at the front of SENDING moves to the end. S is the standard abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: Endings and finales are both the concluding parts of a show, piece of music or story.

clue.text: Poor tenant was wont to be thrifty

definitions.note: the answer is a proverb urging thrift, not a verb phrase

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are in a sorry state and need rearranging

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A hard-up renter who has always been careful with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like part of 'to be thrifty', but it belongs to the anagram letters; the definition is just 'be thrifty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb advises that if you never squander anything you will never go short, which is the essence of frugal living.

clue.text: Very old (50), solider heads north to find accommodation there

definitions.note: plural noun answer for a mass noun

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means travelling upwards, so the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: An ancient soldier trekking to the Arctic in search of somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to 'north': the definition is the kind of lodging found in the far north. 'Very old' looks like one idea but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Igloos are domed snow-block shelters built by Inuit people in Arctic regions, the typical dwelling of the frozen north.

clue.text: Those on the Corinthian omnibus?

blocks.note: surface reading: passengers riding a bus in the Greek city of Corinth
setter's reading: omnibus is Latin for 'for all', and Corinthian means Greek, so it is the Greek phrase for everybody, the many

explanation.surface: Commuters riding a bus around ancient Corinth.
explanation.walkthrough: A bus was originally an omnibus, Latin for 'for all'; the answer is a Greek phrase meaning 'the many', so it is the Greek word for all comers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek-derived phrase means the common people or the masses, everybody in general rather than an elite.

clue.text: Like ABBA? Like a turnip?

blocks.note: first meaning: from Sweden, as the pop group was
second meaning: swede-ish, resembling a swede

explanation.walkthrough: A swede is the British name for the root vegetable Americans call rutabaga, a kind of turnip; the second reading splits the answer as SWEDE-ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: The band came from Sweden, so is Scandinavian by nationality; a turnip-like root resembles a swede in a playful coinage.

clue.text: Wise men heading off for a long time

indicators.note: with the head taken off, the front letter of the word goes

blocks.note: sages are wise men

explanation.surface: The Magi set off on a lengthy journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads as setting out on a journey, but it means removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: 'For ages' is an informal idiom for a very lengthy period, so the plural noun stands for it.

clue.text: Renunciation of stinking acrid slime

indicators.note: something stinking is rotten, and rotten letters fall apart into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone disowning a foul-smelling, sharp-scented ooze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinking' sits naturally beside 'acrid slime' as a description, which hides its job as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclaimer is a formal statement denying responsibility or giving up a claim, which is a renouncing.

clue.text: Single knitted item? Beguiled? Not originally

explanation.surface: Someone charmed by a lone piece of knitwear, wondering if they were ever really captivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' matters: mittens come in pairs, so one item is the singular form.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitten is a hand covering often made of wool on needles, and one of a pair is a single piece.

clue.text: Cheap Italian novelist with no means to be heard

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'No means' reads as poverty, but 'no' stands alone and 'means to be heard' is the microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic can mean inexpensive or offering good value for money, as in an economic price.

clue.text: Digitally alter, very quietly, attractive 'outsize' host – not half, that's accepted

the first half of the four letters

explanation.walkthrough: PP (pianissimo) takes in HOT, OS and HO, giving P-HOTOSHO-P.
explanation.definitionFit: The image-editing software has become a verb for retouching pictures by computer, a trademark used generically.

clue.text: Subsequently, the Scripture lessons at university in progress

blocks.note: taken as written
RE is religious education, the British school subject

explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a subject in British schools; 'up' for being at university is a British idiom, as is 'come down' for leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereupon is a formal adverb meaning immediately after that, so it means afterwards or next in time.

clue.text: A little busy, the French hotel; nothing to write home about

indicators.note: only a small part of the word is wanted, its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: A fairly lively French hotel that was nevertheless unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little busy' reads as 'somewhat crowded' but it takes just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah as an adjective means dull or unexciting, and 'nothing to write home about' is an idiom for mediocre.

clue.text: Witnesses hijack, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

explanation.surface: Bystanders observe a hijacking, according to news reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Witnesses' looks like a noun, people in court; it is the verb, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness an event is to observe it with your own eyes, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Little singer to squabble repeatedly

blocks.note: to spar is to argue or bicker
the same idea given a second time, another word for a quarrel

explanation.surface: A small vocalist prone to constant bickering.

explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small songbird, and birds that sing are commonly called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Extremely professorial tenor, most insipid

clue.text: Everyman's flipping furious in far-off land?

explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, such as those in the Gulf, distant countries from a British view.

explanation.definitionFit: Soulful means expressing deep emotion, so it is a synonym for sincere and deeply felt.
